subject: Medisync DPA — initial redlines & counsel comments
messages:
From: Claire Summers <c.summers@medisync.ai>

Cc: legal@medisync.ai, andrew.park@medisync.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA - initial redlines

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. Attached is our initial redline of Redwood's DPA (Medisync_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx). High-level items our privacy counsel flagged:

- Subprocessors: request mandatory prior notice and 30-day termination right if a subprocessor change is unacceptable (we prefer explicit approval for anything outside the roster).
- International transfers: require EU-US transfer mechanism documented (SCCs preferred).
- Audit & inspection: we need explicit on-site audit right or an option to review third-party SOC2 report.
- Retention & deletion: want guaranteed deletion within 15 days of termination, including backups.
- KMS/Customer-controlled keys: request optional KMS support for PHI-like datasets.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on the above? We reviewed the list of Redwood subprocessors in the call but would like the roster as part of the DPA. We usually execute via DocuSign once redlines settle.

Appreciate a response by EOD PT on 8/18 — our procurement timeline is tight.

Thanks,
Claire Summers
Senior Counsel, Medisync
Medisync, Inc.

Attachment: Medisync_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx (track changes)

From: monica.patel@redwood.com <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA - initial redlines (internal notes)

Internal — drafting notes for response to Medisync redlines. Summary of counsel positions and proposed language:

1) Subprocessors: we cannot accept unilateral approval rights per subprocessor. Proposed compromise: Redwood will provide 30 days' prior notice of material changes to the subprocessor roster and will permit termination if Medisync reasonably objects to a new subprocessor within that period. We will include an exception for emergency replacements with notice within 5 business days.

2) Audit & inspection: Medisync asked for on-site audits. Proposal: supply our latest SOC 2 Type II report plus a right to review documentation and ask for a third-party assessment at customer expense if reasonable suspicion of noncompliance exists. On-site inspections limited to a narrow scope and require 60 days' notice and mutually agreed scope.

3) Retention & deletion: customer wants 15-day deletion including backups. We propose: active data deleted within 30 days; backups deleted within 90 days to allow for disaster recovery and legal holds. If Medisync requires a shorter backup window for regulated data, we can offer a contract add-on.

4) Transfers: we will accept SCCs / EU addendum language. Confirm whether Medisync needs a signed EU-US Addendum or if SCCs are sufficient; we can provide either.

5) KMS: Redwood currently offers customer-managed KMS in our Private deployment and can offer a managed KMS option with an add-on for Hosted. Need to confirm whether Medisync will require this for the initial scope.

I'm attaching a short redline we can send back (redline_response_v1.docx) — it's conservative and keeps most of our standard protections. If any item is commercially sensitive (retention/KMS pricing), Priyom please flag so Aditya can sign off.

Monica Patel
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
Attachment: redline_response_v1.docx

From: Claire Summers <c.summers@medisync.ai>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: andrew.park@medisync.ai, legal@medisync.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA - initial redlines

Monica — thanks for the detailed run-through, that helps. A few clarifications from our side after internal counsel review:

- Audit: Medisync is OK with SOC2 in most cases but reserves the right to request an on-site review for material incidents or if SOC2 evidence is insufficient. We will accept a 30-day notice for on-site requests (we can be flexible on scope).
- Retention: we can accept your active-data/delete timeline of 30 days, but request that backup deletion be "as soon as practicable and no later than 45 days"; can Redwood confirm?
- Subprocessors: 30 days' notice is acceptable. Our ask for explicit termination rights remains but we can limit to material breaches or non-remediable security issues.
- KMS: Medisync would prefer a KMS option for hosted data. Please provide a quote for the add-on and the technical spec (KMS integration, key rotation, logs).

We're trying to avoid multiple back-and-forths — if Redwood can send one consolidated redline with the suggested language above, we'll review and aim to route to DocuSign. Attached is our internal audit requirements summary for your security team (Medisync_audit_reqs.pdf).

Thanks,
Claire

Attachment: Medisync_audit_reqs.pdf

On-site/inspection standard: "reasonable scope" clarified as systems ingesting customer data and relevant controls; 30 days' notice acceptable.

Claire — thanks for the quick turn and for the clarification. Summary of where we are and next steps so there is a single source of truth: 

Agreed / can accept:
- Subprocessor notice: Redwood will provide 30 days' prior notice for new subprocessors; Medisync will have termination rights limited to material breaches/non-remediable security issues. Emergency replacements will follow our emergency notification process.
- Audit baseline: Redwood will provide SOC2 Type II. On-site audits permitted only for material incidents or evidence of noncompliance; on-site requests require 30 days' notice and mutually agreed scope.
- Active data deletion: 30 days after termination.

Open / commercial or need follow-up:
- Backups deletion window: Medisync requested 45 days; Redwood proposed 90 days by default with an add-on for 45 days. Monica, recommend final position (standard vs. paid tighter SLA).
- KMS: Redwood can support customer-managed keys in Private deployments and offer hosted KMS as an add-on. Neha, please provide the KMS spec and an indicative cost for the add-on.

Action items: 
1) Monica to finalize the consolidated redline and send to Medisync by EOD PT 8/18 (redline_response_v1.docx).
2) Neha to attach KMS technical spec and pricing to the DocuSign package if Medisync confirms they want the add-on.
3) Priyom to monitor procurement and approval chain; if Medisync confirms acceptance we'll route to DocuSign (envelope placeholder: https://docusign.com/envelope/12345-abcdef).
